 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 20, 2026, 09:20:29 IST SUMMARY Indian equities's ability to sustain its recent upward momentum will remain in focus, particularly after a sharp recovery in banking and automobile stocks. Foreign fund inflows have emerged as a key support for Indian equities, with monthly investments reaching a record $12.21 billion. 
 However, the broader global environment presents a contrasting picture, as major Asian indices have recorded steep losses amid concerns surrounding technology stocks and the possibility of a US rate hike. Meanwhile, movements in the rupee and international crude prices add another dimension to the market outlook. 
 Investors will also be tracking the performance of heavyweight stocks, sectoral trends and the extent to which domestic equities can hold on to their recent gains. 
 Together, these factors are expected to shape the direction of stock market in the days ahead. Track TOI’s coverage on BSE Sensex and Nifty50 to know which way stock markets are headed: Live Events 
 09:20 (IST) Nov 20 Stock market today: BSE Sensex tumbles over 350 points in early trade, Nifty50 below 25,460 Dalal Street began Friday on a negative note, with both benchmarks shedding in early trade. The Nifty50 was down 97.75 points, or 0.38% while BSE Sensex declined 357.78 points, or 0.43%, to 82,663.97. The weakness comes after 08:58 (IST) Nov 20 Stock market today: Check top stocks to buy on Friday
 Market expert Hitesh Rathi of Angel One has identified three stocks across sectors that investors can keep on their radar, sharing his picks based on technical analysis.
 Read full story › 08:54 (IST) Nov 20 Stock market today: Gift Nifty signals muted opening Dalal Street is expected to see a muted opening, with GIFT Nifty futures trading at 25,352 points against the Nifty50's previous close of 25,514.30. The expected weakness came after domestic indices advanced to nine-month highs, raising the possibility of consolidation amid overbought conditions. The Nifty and Sensex had gained 1.5% and 1.8%, respectively, during the week, putting them on course for their fourth consecutive weekly advance. 
 The recent rally has been supported by strong foreign investor participation, easing crude prices, an unwinding of artificial intelligence-linked trades and upbeat corporate earnings. The market's near-term direction will depend on how these domestic support factors balance against the cautious global sentiment.

 08:54 (IST) Nov 20 Stock market today: Asian equities face sharp losses as AI trade reversal weighs on sentiment Global equity markets presented a contrasting picture, with Asian shares heading towards their worst weekly performance since 2020. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan declined 2.5% on Friday. Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI also recorded steep losses, falling 4.1% and 4.7%, respectively. The declines tracked an overnight slide in Wall Street equities as the reversal in artificial intelligence-linked trades continued. Anthropic's market debut also failed to restore investor confidence in AI-related trades. The weakness across major Asian markets highlighted the cautious global backdrop against which Indian equities were expected to trade. While domestic benchmarks had retained their recent gains, international market movements remained an important factor in assessing the broader investment sentiment. 08:53 (IST) Nov 20 Stock market today: Crude prices edge higher but remain on course for weekly decline International crude oil prices edged higher, although both major benchmarks remained on track to record weekly losses. Brent crude futures rose 24 cents, or 0.3%, to $92.22 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate futures for December gained 19 cents, or 0.2%, to $83.40. The more actively traded January WTI contract advanced 20 cents, or 0.2%, to $82.64. The gains followed renewed concerns over supply disruptions after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. However, Brent was set for a 3.5% weekly decline, while December WTI was headed for a 6% drop. Both benchmarks were also on course for a third consecutive weekly decline. 08:52 (IST) Nov 20 Stock market recap: Rupee rose 9 paise to close at 93.32 against US dollar Rupee also extended its gains for a fourth consecutive session, settling 9 paise higher at 93.32 against the US dollar on Thursday. The currency drew support from a softer greenback and foreign fund inflows amid substantial buying in Indian equities. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.40 and moved between 93.17 and 93.55 during the session before closing at 93.32. However, upward momentum in crude oil prices limited the currency's gains, according to forex traders. The rupee had previously strengthened by 10 paise to close at 93.41 on Wednesday, following gains of 68 paise over the preceding two sessions. The currency's movement reflected the competing influence of foreign inflows, dollar weakness and crude prices. Daily Puzzles

The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 989.94 points, or 1.21%, to settle at 83,021.75. During the session, it had climbed as much as 1,012.06 points, or 1.23%, to touch 83,043.87. 
 The NSE Nifty50 rose 286.35 points, or 1.14%, to close at 25,514.30. The rally was led by automobile and banking stocks, alongside sustained foreign fund inflows and easing commodity prices. The strong session added to the benchmarks' weekly gains and placed them on course for a fourth consecutive week of advances.
 Dalal Street is expected to begin on a cautious note, with benchmarks likely to consolidate after scaling nine-month highs and recording four consecutive weeks of gains. While sustained foreign investor participation, easing commodity prices and upbeat corporate earnings have supported domestic equities, overbought conditions could influence near-term market direction.
Global cues remain mixed, with Asian equities facing pressure amid continued concerns over artificial intelligence-linked trades and the US interest rate outlook. Currency movements and crude oil trends will also remain important factors to watch, particularly as geopolitical developments have renewed concerns over supply disruptions. 
With domestic and international indicators pointing in different directions, the market outlook is likely to reflect a balance between domestic buying support and global uncertainty.
